newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares edge up, seen rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares edge up, seen rangebound.

text.p: Austria's ATX index ended mildly stronger on Thursday after a rangebound session and traders predicted more of the same for the next few days.
"The market is being tweaked slightly upward, but nothing is actually happening," said one trader.
Another described the market as nervous.

"I will only consider it a really important signal when we end above 1,310 or below 1,2800," he said. The market was likely to hover around 1,300 ahead of a possible rate decision by the U.S. Fed next Tuesday, he added.
The blue chip ATX index inched up 0.03 percent to 1,296.28 points. Among its constituents 12 shares rose, eight fell and one was unchanged.
The leading gainer was microchip maker AMS, rising 4.93 percent to 1,019 schillings.
The top loser was brewer BBAG, dropping 2.19 percent to 714 schillings.
Luxury hosiery maker Wolford rebounded on good demand after heavy losses this week. Wolford added 3.31 percent to 1,130 schillings.
The July ATX future climbed five points to 1,306. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
